medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends blood pressure control in CKD; labetalol is pregnancy‑safe antihypertensive per NICE hypertension in pregnancy guidance

medications.purpose: Pre‑eclampsia prophylaxis in a high‑risk pregnant woman with CKD and hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NICE guidance on hypertension in pregnancy (NG136) recommends 75‑150 mg aspirin daily for pre‑eclampsia prevention

medications.purpose: Treat iron‑deficiency anaemia (if confirmed) associated with CKD
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 advises treating anaemia after confirming iron deficiency

medications.duration: Lifelong — review each trimester and adjust to pregnancy targets
medications.purpose: Maintain tight glycaemic control for type 2 diabetes during pregnancy
medications.nice_justification: NICE diabetes guideline (NG28) recommends individualized insulin therapy in pregnancy

treatment_summary: The patient has CKD stage 2 with hypertension, diabetes, and is pregnant. ACE‑I/ARB, SGLT2 inhibitors and statins are contraindicated in pregnancy, so hypertension is managed with labetalol, and low‑dose aspirin is added for pre‑eclampsia prophylaxis. Insulin therapy is continued. Oral iron is prescribed only if iron deficiency is confirmed. All recommendations follow NICE NG203 (CKD management) and relevant pregnancy guidelines, with monitoring of BP, eGFR, ACR, potassium, LFTs, and iron status each trimester.
